concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of palpitations and chest pain, along with the ECG findings of narrow QRS regular tachycardia, support the diagnosis of Supraventricular Tachycardia.
The patient's symptoms of palpitations and chest pain, along with the ECG findings of wide complex irregular tachycardia, support the diagnosis of Ventricular Tachycardia.
The patient's symptoms of palpitations and chest pain, along with the ECG findings of narrow QRS regular tachycardia, could also suggest Atrial Fibrillation.
The patient's symptoms of chest pain, although the Treadmill Stress Test was negative, could suggest Myocardial Ischemia.
The patient's symptoms of lightheadedness and wide complex tachycardia, although the echocardiography was normal, could suggest Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
The patient's symptoms of lightheadedness and wide complex tachycardia, although the echocardiography was normal, could also suggest Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
The patient's symptoms of palpitations and wide complex tachycardia support the diagnosis of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy.
The patient's symptoms of palpitations and wide complex tachycardia, along with the ECG findings, could suggest Long QT Syndrome.

rationales.F01: Palpitations associated with chest pain and lightheadedness suggest a cardiac origin, which could be related to supraventricular or ventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F02: No previous arrhythmic episodes or family history of sudden cardiac death reduces the likelihood of conditions like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy, and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F07: Narrow QRS regular tachycardia triggering a nonsustained phase of wide complex irregular tachycardia is highly suggestive of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F09: Tachycardia with a cycle length of 250 ms revealed by electrophysiology study is indicative of a re-entrant tachycardia, which could be supraventricular or ventricular in origin.
